text:
mike_customer: hey team, we started seeing a spike of 429s and higher tail latency after a traffic burst this morning. Happens when we send ~200 concurrent requests to the text-generation endpoint. We use continuous batching + KV cache. Not sure if we're hitting rate limits or the batcher is queueing and being treated as throttling.

anna_support: sorry to hear that, can you paste one of the failing request ids and a minimal repro config? also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

mike_customer: this is hosted. sample request id in our logs: req=6f4b2c9a, model=r-llama-13b, tokens=800. here's our client config excerpt:```json
{
  "concurrency": 200,
  "batching": { "enabled": true, "max_batch_size": 16, "max_delay_ms": 12 },
  "kv_cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_ms": 300000 },
  "retry": { "max_attempts": 2, "backoff_ms": 100 }
}```

sam_runtime: thanks — that helps. can you also paste a short span from your app logs showing the 429 or the response headers (we look for x-request-id, x-rate-limit-* and x-retry-after)?

mike_customer: log snippet:```
[2026-07-12T09:14:22Z] req=6f4b2c9a start
[2026-07-12T09:14:23Z] req=6f4b2c9a kv_cache MISS
[2026-07-12T09:14:24Z] req=6f4b2c9a queued by batcher (waiting for batch)
[2026-07-12T09:14:30Z] req=6f4b2c9a 429 QuotaExhausted x-request-id=6f4b2c9a x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-retry-after=8
```

luis_sre: two things to distinguish: 429 due to token quota vs internal throttling because the batcher filled and the runtime rejected the request. kv_cache misses cause more tokens to be computed per request which can blow through token-based quotas during bursts.

anna_support: can you confirm if you were on a committed dedicated plan or hosted pay-as-you-go? token quota windows differ.

mike_customer: hosted pay-as-you-go. we assumed hosted would auto-scale for bursts.

sam_runtime: hosted does scale but there are short smoothing windows and per-customer token concurrency protections. Continuous batching can increase per-request compute when there are cache misses because a miss means full compute cost (no KV reuse). If many requests miss KV concurrently, you get a compounding effect: batcher holds requests briefly waiting for batch fill, compute heavy batch runs, and tokens consumed spike -> quota exhausted -> 429s. That looks like what your logs show (miss + queue + 429).

anna_support: quick repro steps for us: 1) send an identical prompt repeatedly to see cache hit rate 2) send a synthetic burst of N parallel requests and share headers 3) include one example request id that failed (you gave 6f4b2c9a already, thanks).

mike_customer: share the synthetic script?

luis_sre: here's a tiny curl-based repro you can run (or we can run if you grant debug access):```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n    -d '{"model":"r-llama-13b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":200}' &
done; wait
```

sam_runtime: while you run that, please also call the trace endpoint with one x-request-id we saw so we can pull server traces: `GET /v1/requests/6f4b2c9a/trace` (console -> support only).

mike_customer: ran the script, attached headers for one failure:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: 6f4b2c9a
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1699691690
x-retry-after: 8
content-type: application/json
```

anna_support: thanks. we're seeing two signals in internal telemetry: a short burst of KV cache miss rate from 5% -> 70% at the time of the spike, and per-customer token throughput briefly exceeded the per-minute window.

sam_runtime: recommended mitigations (short-term):
- reduce client concurrency (e.g., 200 -> 40) and add jitter to avoid synchronized bursts
- reduce max_batch_size (16 -> 4) and max_delay_ms (12 -> 4) so requests are dispatched earlier rather than queued long waiting for full batches
- add client-side warmup to prime KV cache (sequential small requests on cold start)
- respect x-retry-after and implement exponential backoff with jitter

anna_support: medium-term: request a higher burst quota from support (we can apply a temporary increase for hosted customers) or move to Dedicated if you need guaranteed burst capacity. Also enable per-route traces in the console for a day so we can correlate.

mike_customer: curious — why would reducing batch_size help? I thought larger batches were more efficient and cheaper.

luis_sre: good question. larger batches are more efficient when latency distribution is steady and KV cache hit rate is high. But during a sudden burst with cold cache, large batches accumulate many heavy requests that drive token consumption and cause quota exhaustion faster. Smaller batches send some requests earlier which spreads compute over time and reduces peak tokens in a window. It's a tradeoff between cost and hitting smoothing/throttles.

sam_runtime: we also tweaked one internal knob for you: we temporarily lowered your batcher.max_batch_size to 6 for the impacted pool and observed fewer 429s while still keeping reasonable throughput. We also prewarmed popular prefixes.

mike_customer: did that change already? I'm seeing green in our app, 200s returning now, latency down from 1.8s p95 to 620ms p95. thanks.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: changes applied to customer-pool-42 (batcher.max_batch_size=6) by sam_runtime at 2026-07-12T10:08:02Z :rocket:

anna_support: can you monitor for another 24h and let us know if it recurs? If you're still seeing problems we can either extend the config change, raise hosted burst quota, or move you to a reserved burst window on Dedicated.

mike_customer: will monitor. a couple follow-ups: is there a recommended warmup traffic pattern?

luis_sre: yes — 1) send a small number of sequential requests for the hot prefixes (5-10 sequential requests per prefix) 2) avoid all clients simultaneously doing full-scale bursts at startup 3) if you have predictable traffic spikes, pre-warm by running low-rate synthetic requests 60s before the spike

sam_runtime: final note — we recorded the trace for req=6f4b2c9a and attached a short diag in the support ticket. Key takeaway: KV MISS -> larger batch formed -> long compute -> token window hit -> 429. Fixes above addressed the behaviour.

mike_customer: perfect, thanks everyone. closing on our side if it stays stable. appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

anna_support: marking this thread resolved for now. reopen if you get new examples.
